text: For rolling endurance rides, athlete and coach agreed to climb steadily without surging, using conversational breathing and comfortable cadence to regulate effort.
A final riser felt unusually hard, but the athlete and coach attributed it to a headwind after a long day on the feet rather than a negative fitness trend.
For exposed headwind sections, athlete will tuck lower and move snacks earlier to stabilize final-hour energy, while monitoring hands and shoulders during longer low-position stints.
Mild leg heaviness on day two of back-to-back rides cleared after 20 minutes of easy spinning; no plan adjustment was needed.
Plan remains unchanged, but if second-day leg heaviness lasts beyond 30 minutes, the athlete will shorten that ride rather than push through and deepen fatigue.
For rides over two hours, athlete will target one bottle per hour, food every 30 minutes, and a larger breakfast before sustained climbing; the routine will first be practiced on easy rides.
A recovery route with fewer junctions allowed relaxed breathing throughout and made genuinely easy riding easier to maintain.
Recovery spins will start from the park side of town going forward, and easy days will be protected even during busy weeks.

Keep this week as written: current Form is +7 and reported mild leg heaviness has been clearing within 20 minutes. Shorten the second back-to-back day if heaviness lasts beyond 30 minutes, and avoid prolonged low-bar positioning if hand or shoulder discomfort develops.
